title: Abramson Cancer Center Support Grant
text:
Cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States and prevalent in the ethnically diverse
catchment area of the Abramson Cancer Center (ACC), which consists of 12 contiguous counties in
Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Delaware, in which 81 ,4% of ACC's patients reside, Through our Research
Programs and Community Outreach and Engagement, the ACC addresses the burden imposed by highly
prevalent cancers in the catchment area, including breast, prostate, lung, colorectal, melanoma, and
lymphoma, ACC basic, clinical, and population science research - along with Community Outreach and
Engagement Activities - are integrated to prevent, diagnose, and treat these cancers and address cancer risk
factors to promote healthy living,

title: Ultra-Low Field MRI for Assessment of Congenital Heart Disease
text:
Congenital heart disease is a prevalent group of birth defects associated with lifelong comorbidities and surgical
interventions, requiring frequent non-invasive monitoring of cardiovascular anatomy and function. While cardiac
magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) is the most versatile imaging modality for assessing these patients,
conventional high-field CMR (at magnetic field strengths of 1-3 Tesla) faces critical challenges including safety
concerns, high system costs, and image artifacts resulting from metallic implants. To address these challenges,
we will develop CMR on an ultra-low field (ULF) 0.047 Tesla magnet, use artificial intelligence methods to
dramatically enhance image quality, and assess reliability and robustness compared to standard high-field
CMR.

title: A multi-level mass spectrometry pipeline for the analysis of whole proteoforms and their complexes
text:
At the molecular level, the homeostasis of cells and tissues largely depends on the correct activity
of properly structured proteins, that if altered can lead to the onset of a myriad different human
diseases. With this research program we will develop new mass spectrometry technologies for
the analysis of intact protein forms, or proteoforms, and their bioactive complexes, to elucidate
the precise set of genetic and chemical modifications responsible for aberrant phenotypes in the
human population. These new analytical tools will help advancing our understanding of the
mechanisms underlying human pathologies and facilitate the identification of new biomarkers.

title: Mitochondrial Impact on Inflammaging and Cognitive Impairment in HIV and Substance Use
text:
People with HIV (PWH) experience accelerated immune aging and cognitive impairment driven
by chronic inflammation, immune activation, and persistent low-grade viremia, collectively
termed inflammaging. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a central contributor, yet the relationship
between mitochondrial genetic variation, mitochondrial function, immune dysfunction, and
cognitive impairment remains poorly understood. This proposal leverages longitudinal data and
specimens from the AIDS Linked to the Intravenous Experience (ALIVE) cohort to evaluate how
mitochondrial function and genetic variation influence immune and cognitive outcomes.

title: Determinants of oral anaphylaxis to food
text:
In its most severe form, food allergy can trigger life-threatening anaphylaxis. We recently discovered that
susceptibility to oral anaphylaxis is driven by intestinal permeability to food allergens and that this permeability
is genetically regulated and potentially treatable by drugs. We aim to discover the specific mechanisms
controlling gut permeability in order to (1) identify new drugs to prevent anaphylaxis upon ingestion of allergens
and (2) discover diagnostic markers that can identify individuals most at risk of anaphylaxis to food.

title: Core C: Data Analytics Core
text:
The Data Analytics Core will provide biostatistics, bioinformatics, and data management support to all three 
SPORE projects, the CEP and DRP, as well as to the SPORE Cores. The Core will ensure that the appropriate 
statistical design is incorporated into all studies from inception, that the data are properly analyzed using the 
state-of-the-art data methods, and that all results are interpreted on statistical as well as biological significance. 
The Core also supports the SPORE through a state-of-the-art data management platform.

title: Myeloid lineage commitment during stress hematopoiesis
text:
Hematopoiesis refers to the production of various blood cell types, including immune cells, whose generation
can be increased upon demand, e.g. during infection. While critical for immune defense, inappropriate
production of certain immune cells can also drive inflammation pathology, as observed in a growing number of
diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and stroke. Using in vitro experiments and newly established in vivo
mouse models, we will investigate in this project the molecular mechanisms that control immune cell
production and, possibly, can be manipulated to prevent inflammation pathology.

title: OPTIMISE: A Shared Care Approach for Improving Comprehensive Care of Cancer Patients with Comorbidities in A Safety-Net System
text:
Medically underserved patients have the highest burden of multiple chronic conditions and are at increased risk
for poor outcomes during and after cancer treatment. As medically underserved complex cancer patients may
lack healthcare knowledge and access to supportive care, their health outcomes and care transitions might be
improved by enhancing communication and collaboration between their oncologists and primary care providers
(PCPs). This study tests and evaluates a novel shared care model for complex cancer survivors called
OPTIMISE that shifts the timing of thinking about survivorship to point of diagnosis and seeks to develop a clinical
infrastructure to support continuity of care from cancer diagnosis through post-treatment survivorship.

title: Understanding hematopoietic stem cell dysfunction in refractory Crohn's disease
text:
While CD therapies seemingly encompass distinct therapeutic mechanisms, all target the inflammatory response
supporting that medically refractory CD involves mechanisms not directly related to inflammation. We suggest
that refractory disease is due to dysfunction of hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) that reinforce differentiation of
aberrant myeloid cells unable to support intestinal healing and rendering immunotherapy ineffective. This
proposal will explore how to circumvent treatment non-response through cellular and regenerative therapies
outside of traditional approaches that only target inflammation and generate valuable datasets for the research
community to the benefit of a vulnerable population of refractory CD patients.

title: Development of an early detection test for Type 1 Diabetes via NGS-based analysis of β cells-specific methylation patterns in cfDNA
text:
There are currently no biomarkers for the early, highly specific detection of β cell death during the pathogenesis
of Type 1 Diabetes (T1D), as islet autoantibodies can only predict disease risk with limited specificity and cannot
inform on the rate of β cell loss. Building on our successful Phase I identification of thousands of candidate
pancreatic islet-specific methylation markers and development of a validated 50-plex amplicon panel, this Phase
II study will refine these markers to achieve β cell-specificity and scale our amplicon-based NGS platform to 500-
1000 targets for clinical implementation. The goal is to complete analytical and clinical validation of our early T1D
detection test using cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation analysis, enabling CLIA laboratory establishment and
commercialization as the first laboratory-developed test for pre-symptomatic T1D detection.

title: Evaluating Neutralizing Immune Responses to the Essential Invasion Protein RIPR across Human Plasmodium Species
text:
(Revised)
Malaria continues to be a significant global health challenge, posing risks to US travelers and the US military. My project will evaluate the cross-strain and cross-species inhibitory activity of a novel blood-stage malaria vaccine candidate (RIPR) using a combination of ex vivo clinical isolates and CRISPR/Cas9-edited Plasmodium parasites. My results will lead to a better molecular understanding of red blood cell invasion pathways conserved among human pathogenic Plasmodium species and inform the rational design of cross-protective blood-stage malaria vaccines.

title: Synaptic plasticity across the lifespan
text:
As the brain matures, synapses undergo dramatic changes that determine how neurons communicate with one
another. One structure near synapses, the dendritic spine apparatus, influences synaptic communication and is
dysfunctional in multiple neurological disorders. The proposed research aims to determine whether the spine
apparatus and a related structure, the axon cisternal organelle, stabilize and enhance synapses during
development and long-term potentiation, a cellular mechanism of learning and memory.

title: Impact of NK Cells on Control of BK Polyomavirus
text:
The human polyomavirus BK (BKPyV) infects most people for life but only causes diseases in persons with a
compromised immune system, such as kidney transplant recipients. BKPyV reactivation can result in the loss of
the transplanted kidney. There is currently no effective treatment against BKPyV. Natural killer (NK) cells help
the body defend itself against viral infections, and the proposed studies will determine how NK cells contribute
to the control of diseases caused by BKPyV. The outcome of these studies will guide the development of novel
NK cell-based therapies to protect persons with a reduced ability to fight infectious diseases against BKPyV.

title: Air Pollutant Transformation of Indoor Allergens
text:
Indoor and outdoor air pollution contribute to chronic pulmonary, cardiovascular, and other diseases and ac-
count for millions of deaths worldwide. While much is known about the direct effects of these pollutants on hu-
man airway health, the indirect effects of air pollution on inhaled allergens and other particulates are not well
understood. This project will investigate how common reactive chemicals in indoor air alter house dust mite, an
ordinary component of house dust, to modify its ability to trigger allergic inflammation.

title: Macromolecular Structure and Mechanism of Innate Immune Complexes
text:
This research advances our understanding of fundamental biological processes by investigating how the innate
immune sensor NLRP3 recognizes oxidized mitochondrial DNA to initiate inflammation. It contributes to the
NIGMS mission by revealing new mechanisms of nucleic acid sensing, protein-DNA interaction, and
inflammasome regulation. The resulting insights could open novel avenues for drug discovery, but the focus of
this work is on mechanistic biology using structural and biochemical approaches.

title: NeuroHIV and Community Partnership and Disparity Core for Institution # 269291
text: Despite many people with HIV (PWH) having well-suppressed infection with antiretroviral treatment (ART), some populations of PWH do not engage in the HIV care continuum from timely HIV diagnosis to viral suppression. The delay in the initiation of ART and disruptions to HIV care and ART adherence, may place some at further risk of neuroHIV-related complications, including neurocognitive impairments and neurobehavioral sequelae as well as other comorbid clinical problems. Reducing the number of people not engaged in care is an important goal of the National HIV/AIDS Strategy. The Comprehensive NeuroHIV Center (CNHC) is well-positioned not only to support research that addresses the mechanisms of neuroHIV, but also how to facilitate exciting interdisciplinary collaborations to investigate, prevent, treat, and address engagement differences that may contribute significantly to neuroHIV-related disease. By supporting a community-engaged research paradigm, the CNHC will maximize the impact of neuroHIV scientists’ research for populations not engaged in care, while leveraging community members’ expertise about their needs, strengths, and experiences. Thus, in this renewal, we have initiated the NeuroHIV Community Partnership Core (NHCPC) to foster community- partnership and interdisciplinary collaborations that examine, address, and prevent non-engagement that may result in neuroHIV complications. The NHCPC will aim to (1) conduct a community needs assessment to refine the Core’s research infrastructure services; (2) serve as a primary resource to guide competent research that engages communities and addresses neuroHIV; and (3) disseminate research findings in bidirectional communication with the local and broader community to address neuroHIV. The NHCPC will work in synergy with the Central Administrative and Management Core to complement its support by aiding research involving neuroHIV disparities; the Developmental Research and Mentorship Core to support all researchers and NHCPC-related studies; and the Clinical and Translational Research Support Core to enhance its services for competent research and expand its recruitment efforts involving all groups at greater risk of developing neuroHIV; and all Cores, including the Viral Gene Editing and Bioinformatics Core and the Cell Biology and Functional Analysis Core, to help disseminate findings and facilitate community awareness and involvement with respect to the development of neuroHIV. The Core will increase the number of interdisciplinary collaborations and resulting studies and publications. In synergy with the other Cores, the NHCPC will enhance the quality of the neuroHIV research enterprise by supporting research related to neuroHIV and the continuum of HIV care to prevent, treat, and understand neuroHIV disease.

title: Computational Modeling of the Interplay between External Signaling and Transcription Rewiring using Spatial Transcriptomics and Single Cell Multiome Data
text:
This proposal aims to create a series of new statistical methods to help us better utilize genetic scores in the 
study of the causes behind intricate human diseases. It will incorporate multi-omics data to facilitate molecularlyinformed disease pathways and assess the impact of each pathway on the disease, and also use family-based 
studies to provide unbiased investigations of how multiple correlated environmental factors or biomarkers 
influence diseases. It will further provide easy-to-use software tools and a summary statistics database for 
researchers to analyze large-scale multi-modal data to accelerate future research, enabling a more 
comprehensive and unbiased understanding of how molecular changes contribute to human diseases.

title: Nanobodies for Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection
text:
Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health burden, with approximately 250 million
people chronically infected and at increased risk for liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Our goal is to
develop and characterize single-domain antibodies (nanobodies) that target the HBV surface antigen as a
therapeutic strategy for chronic HBV infection.

title: Molecular Devices for the Detection and Treatment of HCMV Infection
text:
CMV has a high global prevalence and is the leading cause of transplant related mortality. The proposed
research will combine tools from DNA and protein based synthetic structural biology to construct (i) a biosensor
that will allow transplant patients to self-screen for CMV at home, and (ii) a protein switch that will use CMV’s
genetic signature to kill virally infected cells. This is the first attempt at combining technologies from two separate
fields that have evolved independently, and the outcome of this project will pave the way for the construction of
biomolecular switches using this hybrid approach for applications beyond the reach of each individually.

title: Neuronal and Vascular Interactions in the Visual System
text:
(PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE)
Impaired neurovascular coupling (NVC) often precedes and perpetuates symptoms of neurodegenerative
diseases, particularly within the visual system. Understanding and identifying the critical cellular and molecular
mechanisms that underlie NVC will advance the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of such diseases,
ultimately improving the treatment of vision loss in humans. Specifically, the tools and databases developed,
along with the knowledge acquired through this research, will expedite progress in the understanding and
treatment of diseases such as glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration (AMD),
retinal vein occlusion, and other neurodegenerative diseases affecting the visual cortex, including Alzheimer’s
Disease.
